# ROM-editor coverage ledger

This is the authoritative per-system support matrix and the derived counts for `DRAGONBYTE-Z-ROM-EDITOR-COVERAGE-001`. It renders `docs/research/rom_editor_coverage.json`, which is normative: every state, count and per-row dimension below is read from that file, and `docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_SYSTEM_CENSUS.md` carries the evidence narrative.

Baseline `486e3c665929a8dc57c63b7915f74606e30ccb0d` (origin/master, clean). The fixed product-capability registry `src/data/capabilities.json` is a separate record: 24 capabilities, all state `shipped`, 13 `proof: runtime` and 11 `proof: application`. It is read, not modified, and it is not this denominator.

## 1. Schema

The machine-readable artifact is `docs/research/rom_editor_coverage.json`, schema version 1. Determinism: Rows are grouped by area in a fixed order (MAP/WORLD, ENTITIES/GAMEPLAY, SCRIPT/TEXT, GRAPHICS, AUDIO, SYSTEM/ROM) and hold the order the census enumerated them. Every list is sorted where it is a set of names. No timestamp, host path or run-specific value is stored. Every count in totals and rom_surface is recomputed from rows by tests/unit/test_rom_editor_coverage.py, which fails on any difference; no count is authored by hand.

Fields:

- `rows[].id` - stable census id, kebab-case, unique across the file
- `rows[].area` - MAP/WORLD | ENTITIES/GAMEPLAY | SCRIPT/TEXT | GRAPHICS | AUDIO | SYSTEM/ROM
- `rows[].games.<game>.state` - one of vocabularies.coverage_states; the row's current top-level coverage state for that title
- `rows[].games.<game>.basis` - MEASURED (this title was investigated and the cell is supported by evidence) | NOT_INVESTIGATED (no adequate evidence for this title exists; the state is a statement about this lab, not about the game)
- `rows[].games.<game>.engine_knowledge` - one of vocabularies.engine_knowledge
- `rows[].games.<game>.runtime_evidence` - one of vocabularies.runtime_evidence
- `rows[].games.<game>.confidence` - CONFIRMED | INFERRED | UNKNOWN, per docs/research-conventions.md
- `rows[].read|edit|author|xref|raw_range|validation_rebuild|ui|restrictions|external_tool` - row-level prose; each names the title when the titles differ
- `facilities[]` - generic ROM-editor facilities. Deliberately NOT part of denominator.accepted_rows: a facility is a product capability, not a game system.
- `totals` - computed strictly from rows[].games; a cell whose state is N_A is excluded from that title's denominator. by_area_buus_fury counts this title's cells only, so its state columns sum to its row count.

Vocabularies:

- `coverage_states`: `FULLY_EDITABLE`, `PARTIALLY_EDITABLE`, `SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY`, `KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED`, `UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED`, `N_A`
- `engine_knowledge`: `PROVEN`, `SUBSTANTIAL`, `PARTIAL`, `MINIMAL`, `UNKNOWN`
- `runtime_evidence`: `PROVEN`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION`, `NEEDED`, `UNKNOWN`
- `basis`: `MEASURED`, `NOT_INVESTIGATED`
- `confidence`: `CONFIRMED`, `INFERRED`, `UNKNOWN`

Coverage-state definitions:

- `FULLY_EDITABLE` - Inspectable, safely editable, validated against known-invalid writes, persisted through project and build, not restricted to a subset that materially changes ordinary hacking of that system, and observed in the governed emulator; where a runtime observation is impossible for the domain, the state is PARTIALLY_EDITABLE with that reason stated.
- `PARTIALLY_EDITABLE` - The product can semantically modify the system and material restrictions remain; the restriction is named numerically where a number exists.
- `SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY` - The product identifies and displays the system and no semantic write path reaches it. Raw hex editing does not count.
- `KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED` - The system is identified and bounded enough to say what it is, and the product has no semantic model for it.
- `UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED` - An editor-relevant region or system is known or plausibly held to exist and its semantic role or boundary is not understood well enough to classify it, or it has been measured only as a negative over declared tables. A measured negative is not a proven boundary.
- `N_A` - Evidence shows the system genuinely does not exist in that title.

## 2. Denominator

One row per coherent editor-relevant semantic domain: a structure, resource family or engine system whose support can meaningfully be classified, with a boundary that evidence supports. A row is not a map, not a function, not a capability and not a UI surface. Rows were enumerated before any count was taken; the count in totals is computed, never chosen.

Accepted rows: **40**. The family-wide aggregate counts (row, game) cells, not rows: one cell per row per title. A cell whose state is N_A is excluded from both numerator and denominator. Because the state vocabulary is ordinal only for FULLY_EDITABLE and PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (the two states in which the product can write), the only aggregate percentage published is writable_cells / measured_cells; the five state counts are published separately per title and never summed into one score.

Seed areas the census investigated and did **not** turn into rows:

- **collision** - Measured on Buu's Fury only: this title keeps no separate per-map collision table, so collision is not a distinct editor-relevant structure in it. The game certainly has walls; the finding is that they are not carried by a collision table of their own. Nothing is claimed for LOGII or LOG1. Evidence: tests/integration/test_local_collision_rom.py:214
- **inventory** - Not established as a ROM structure. The two item index lists the consumer FUN_080164d0 builds are runtime state in an object at +0x134 and +0x284, and a runtime structure is not a ROM-editable domain. Evidence: FUN_080164d0 (ROM decompilation)
- **unowned proven strides** - A 20-byte-stride table at 0x083BB78C and a 33-byte pool at 0x083BBBB0 are bounded in stride and have no found consumer. An unexplained stride is not a system until a consumer exists, so they get no row. Evidence: 0x083BB78C and 0x083BBBB0 (ROM bytes); no inbound code reference found
- **world map** - No world-map table, region or consumer was established in any title. Evidence: Ghidra lane: symbol-name search returned empty and no byte search exists; no tracked research document names one
- **encounters and spawn logic** - No separate encounter or spawn table was found; spawns are carried by the per-area object arrays that row area-object-array-tables covers. Evidence: docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md; 0x08008b30 array walk
- **boss definitions** - No boss classification exists in the project and none was established in the image; bosses are not a separate structure with its own boundary. Evidence: tools/webfoot/enemy_randomizer/eligibility.py:18-24
- **RNG** - No engine RNG state or table was established; the project has randomizer seeds, which are product inputs. Evidence: tools/webfoot/randomizer/service.py:188; no engine RNG evidence found
- **effects and projectiles as a source system** - No separate deterministic effect definition system was found; effects ride the sprite pipeline. Evidence: docs/research/GRAPHICS_COVERAGE.md
- **cutscene art as a separate family** - No evidence separates cutscene art from the title and static screen family. Evidence: docs/research/GRAPHICS_COVERAGE.md (TITLE/STATIC/CUTSCENE UNRESOLVED as one load list)
- **overlays and code loading** - The platform is the GBA, which has no overlay mechanism; the relocation layer is a codec over anchors, not a runtime loader. Evidence: tools/research/domain_reachability.py:417-418
- **compiler-embedded source paths and assert strings** - Real and proven at four sites, but it is build debris that names compilation units, not a system an editor would expose on its own; it is recorded as census evidence. Evidence: ROM 0x08004160, 0x08004818, 0x08008A5C, 0x08013BAC

## 5. Per-row dimensions

### Map and world data

#### `map-entry-records`

**Map identity and header records** - The per-area record the engine's own key lookup reads: 452 records of 56 bytes at 0x0808E2E0. Carries the two-byte map key the engine searches by, the metadata fields the SDK exposes, and pointers to the area's object arrays.

- **Semantic read:** All 452 records enumerate. The key, the five metadata fields the SDK names (zone, area, variation, flags, music_id) and the leading counts read. LOGII: a real 0x38-stride table exists at 0x08409368 with the same two-leading-byte key shape and ROM pointers in its +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 slots, and the profile deliberately does not declare it against this codec; field-level identity is UNKNOWN.
- **Existing-record edit:** Five metadata fields are writable through tools/webfoot/maps.py set_field with a per-field range table; identity sharing is refused by measured exclusive-ownership checks. No Workbench surface calls set_field, so field editing is SDK and CLI only.
- **New-record authoring:** New rows are authorable: the build re-emits the whole table above the original end, repoints the one literal the key lookup loads and raises the compiled row bound. Ceiling 58 appended rows, runtime-observed.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Inbound: the key lookup at 0x08008A58, the linear key scan in FUN_080089fc, the map list, the Atlas index. Outbound: the per-area object-array pointers and the trailing per-area pointer.
- **Raw backing range:** file 0x08E2E0..0x0945C0 = image 0x0808E2E0..0x080945C0, 25,312 bytes, 452 x 0x38.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Build re-emits the table and the compiled bound; project validate refuses an index-moving change by name. Byte-exact round trip of canonical records is proven by the profile reader.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor lists and renders every map; New map is a shipped surface. Field-level header editing has no UI.
- **Known restrictions:** Record fields +0x0C, +0x10, +0x18, +0x1C, +0x20, +0x24, +0x28, +0x30 and +0x34 are not modelled; the trigger semantics some tracked notes place at +0x04 and +0x10 are disputed (see map-event-trigger-records). New-row authoring is capped at 58 rows and an authored row inherits its donor.
- **External tool currently required:** hex editor for the unmodelled fields; Ghidra to settle the disputed offsets.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge MINIMAL, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence INFERRED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x0808E2E0 and record 10 at 0x0808E510; consumer FUN_080089fc with stride 0x38 and the key-lookup literal 0x08008A58 = 0x0808E2E0; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:45-48
- **Open research questions:** Which of +0x0C..+0x34 are counts, pointers or flags? Is the 0x08409368 LOGII table the same record family in a variant layout?
- **Evidence references:** 0x0808E2E0 (ROM bytes); FUN_080089fc (stride 0x38); 0x08008A58 literal = 0x0808E2E0; tools/webfoot/maps.py:625; tools/webfoot/project/model.py:80,118; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:45-48; docs/research/MAP_NEW_AUTHORING.md

#### `map-layout-chunk-grids`

**Map layout chunk grids** - A map's layers and the fixed-size grid of four-byte chunk references inside each layer record, which is what the engine draws as the map's visible layout.

- **Semantic read:** All 452 maps and 1,808 layer slots enumerate; 1,516 slots are the dominant chunk-grid form. Cell values, layer pointers and classification are read and rendered.
- **Existing-record edit:** 440 of 452 maps expose an editable layer; a cell is reassigned in place to another chunk a dominant layer of the same map already uses. Painting, undo and eyedropper are one history. 12 maps are refused for three named reasons: single-chunk dominant grids, absent dominant layers, forms outside the proven grid (screen-entry layers, the terrain-field form used by map 19, zero-dimension records).
- **New-record authoring:** Growth only: a supported layer's grid may be enlarged and re-emitted above the original end with the layer-slot pointer repointed, and the map extent word raised. Shrinking is refused. One unused layer slot may be activated with a new supported visual layer.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Map identity to layer records to chunk containers; Atlas lists the layer and cell owners; the renderer resolves cells through the map's assembled character block.
- **Raw backing range:** Layer records and their grids are addressed per layer from the map root; no single table. The chunk-container table reached from the grid is row map-chunk-containers.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate plus build; the application round-trip reopens the emitted image through its own manifest. Emulator validation of the layout-write capability itself was not performed; the painting and resize capabilities were.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Layout mode: grid view, cell replacement, chunk chooser, resize form, layer list, Create Chunk.
- **Known restrictions:** The writable unit is a four-byte chunk reference, not a hardware tile. A map whose dominant layers between them hold a single chunk has nothing to paint with; a layer that draws one chunk on its own is editable from a sibling's. No new graphics reach a layer: only arrangements of chunks the layer already draws. Authored grids are map-scoped. The runtime evidence on this row comes from the painted-cell authority, which writes the same four-byte cell and was observed after leaving and re-entering the area; the registry's layout capability separately records that emulator validation of its own single-operation write was not performed, so the two records must not be quoted as one.
- **External tool currently required:** tile editor plus a custom decoder for anything below the chunk: tileset entries, tile bits 12-15 and palettes outside the shared object palette.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/map_layout_edit.py:63-76; tests/integration/test_map_layout_editor_rom.py:55-62 (452/440/12); runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:185 (tiles) and :219 (resize)
- **Open research questions:** What do tile-map bits 12-15 mean (they are zero in all 3,834,880 canonical entries and are preserve-only)? Map 19 uses the terrain-field layer form that the editor refuses; whether a background ever displays its composite plane is provisional and waits on a map-19 fixture, not on tooling (docs/research/ASSET_EXPORT_MAP19_VERIFICATION.md:380-449).
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/map_layout_edit.py:63-76; tools/webfoot/map_layout_write.py:38; tools/webfoot/map_resize.py; tests/integration/test_map_layout_editor_rom.py:56-58,162-168; src/data/capabilities.json:157-194,213-229

#### `map-chunk-containers`

**Map chunk containers** - The engine's chunk resource: a 32x32 plane of 16-bit screen entries that a layout cell refers to by address. This is the level at which map graphics are composed in this engine.

- **Semantic read:** Chunk bodies are reached through the layer grid and are rendered; the chunk's 16-bit entries are decoded for display.
- **Existing-record edit:** Existing chunks are readable but the shipped surface composes new ones rather than editing retail ones in place.
- **New-record authoring:** A new chunk may be created from one a dominant layer already draws: its 32x32 plane is rearranged using only screen entries that same layer already displays, it gets its own project identity, and the build materialises it above the original ROM end. Runtime-observed: the engine's loaded BG1 tilemap carries the authored arrangement while BG0, BG2 and BG3 stay byte-identical.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Layer grid cell to chunk address; chunk to the map's assembled character block that resolves its tile ordinals.
- **Raw backing range:** Chunk bodies are addressed per map; a new body is emitted above the original ROM end through the allocator.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate refuses an entry outside the layer's own vocabulary; build allocates and resolves the cell. Runtime-proven for the authored case.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Layout mode: Create Chunk, chunk editor, chunk brush.
- **Known restrictions:** An authored chunk adds no tiles and no palettes: it is a new arrangement of graphics the map already draws. Chunks are map-scoped because their tile ordinals only resolve through one map's character block. Creation depends on generated expansion, since the canonical image declares 256 bytes of free space.
- **External tool currently required:** tile editor and a graphics codec writer for genuinely new artwork.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/map_chunk.py; docs/research/MAP_CHUNK_AUTHORING.md; runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:195-211
- **Open research questions:** Is a chunk body ever shared between maps, and what would make one portable?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/map_chunk.py; docs/research/MAP_CHUNK_AUTHORING.md; src/data/capabilities.json:195-211

#### `map-graphics-tilesets`

**Map graphics: character blocks, tilesets and screen-entry planes** - The assembled graphics a map's chunk entries index: the character block, the tileset and the palettes a layer draws with. Distinct from chunk containers, which hold only references into this vocabulary.

- **Semantic read:** The tileset census and atlas commands enumerate a map's graphics, and the compositor renders them. The proven render path covers maps 39 and 40; the general case is not proven, which is the main limit on this row's read side.
- **Existing-record edit:** None. No SDK writer addresses a tileset or a character-block entry.
- **New-record authoring:** None. No shipped surface composes new tiles or tilesets.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Chunk to character block; the map record to its graphics; Atlas carries the owners.
- **Raw backing range:** Character-block and tileset bodies are addressed per map; the renderer resolves them from the map record.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable at this state: there is no write path to validate.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Layout mode renders chunk cells; there is no tile or tileset surface.
- **Known restrictions:** Read coverage itself is partial: proven for two maps. Tile-map bits 12-15 are zero in every canonical entry and must be preserved by any future writer, which needs no semantics. Palettes are shared with the object palette system.
- **External tool currently required:** standalone tile or graphics editor plus a custom decoder; the compressed container format also needs the encoder that row compression-codec covers.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/formats/map_graphics.py; tools/webfoot/tileset_compositor.py; tools/research/domain_reachability.py:366 (proven render for maps 39 and 40 only); tools/webfoot/cli.py:618-643
- **Open research questions:** What is the full map-graphics load list, and why does only maps 39/40 render?

#### `area-object-array-tables`

**Per-area counted object array tables** - The engine loads four independent counted arrays per area, each reached through the map record's +0x04 pointer: a count byte per family in the pointed-to structure and an array pointer per family at +0x14 (stride 4), +0x18 (stride 4), +0x1C (stride 4) and +0x20 (stride 8). This is the structural answer to what the unmodelled sibling records are.

- **Semantic read:** One of the four arrays is enumerated and rendered by the product. The existence of the other three is proven, but the product has no reader for their elements.
- **Existing-record edit:** Array +0x14 is editable through the placement surfaces. Arrays +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 have no reader and no writer.
- **New-record authoring:** Clone-only for array +0x14, ceiling 255 object slots per map. The other three arrays have no authoring path.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Map record +0x04 to the object block; the object block's four counts and array pointers; placement records to the sprite resolver and the enemy stat table.
- **Raw backing range:** The array pointers are per area; the map-10 array is at file 0x07293C. No fixed table bounds the whole family.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Array +0x14 writing validates and builds and is runtime-proven. The other three arrays participate in no validation because nothing writes them.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Objects mode and the Scene editor both operate on array +0x14 only.
- **Known restrictions:** Structure confidence on the count bytes and on the pointed-to structure's base is PARTIAL rather than PROVEN: the decompiled walk dereferences map+0x04 before reading a count, while a tracked note places counts directly on the map record, and the same lane that produced the four-array claim separately found the 0x08008B30 map-loader attribution wrong, so the four-array model is INFERRED and disputed rather than settled. Three of four families are unmodelled, which is the largest single map-system coverage gap found. The row's writable cell is shared: the write path named in edit is the placement path of row placement-records, and the aggregate rule prints a shared-path caveat for it.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to decode the element types of the +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 families; hex editor to read them now.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PARTIAL, runtime PROVEN, confidence INFERRED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** FUN_08008b30 decompilation and the inline walk at 0x08008C9E..0x08008CAE; ROM bytes at 0x08008CA2 (ldrb r0,[r0,#0x4]) and 0x08008CAC (ldr r0,[r0,#0x14]); docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md
- **Open research questions:** What are the +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 arrays: warps, spawns, triggers, decorations? Is the count byte base the map record or the structure +0x04 points at?
- **Evidence references:** 0x08008b30 (ROM decompilation); 0x08008C9E..0x08008CAE (ROM bytes); docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md:15

#### `warps-transitions`

**Warps and map transitions** - The records that carry the player between areas: 735 transition records across nineteen or more classes, with the 566 class covering most of them.

- **Semantic read:** All 735 records are enumerated and round-trip byte-exactly with no anomalies. Trigger regions are drawn on the map.
- **Existing-record edit:** Destination, arrival position and facing are retargetable for the supported classes; bytes with unresolved meaning (+0x13 and the low nibble of +0x10) are preserved and not editable.
- **New-record authoring:** A transition the image does not contain can be authored from a same-map class-566 template with an expanded record-pointer array above the original end. Runtime-proven: a human-operated run consumed an authored transition.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Map to map through destinations; transition to its trigger region on the canvas; the Warps list selects on the canvas.
- **Raw backing range:** The record array is reached from the map's connection root; record-array bases are in the pointer-table infrastructure row.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate plus build; a shared connection root or an unsupported class fails closed with its reason. Runtime-proven for creation.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Warps mode, plus canvas trigger regions with drag-to-move.
- **Known restrictions:** The 169-class family is refused for retargeting and creation because its stored arrival is a scene-relative delta. A map sharing its connection root is refused. No deletion exists. A stale staged creation has no per-row discard.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra for the 169-class arrival semantics and the two unresolved byte fields; hex editor otherwise.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/formats/map_transitions.py; tools/webfoot/map_transitions.py; tests pinning 735 records; runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:232-253
- **Open research questions:** What does the 169-class arrival delta compose against? What selects through 0x03001A34, which read zero on every runtime sample?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/map_transitions.py; tools/webfoot/formats/map_transitions.py; src/data/capabilities.json:232-253; docs/research/MAP_WARPS_AND_CONNECTIONS.md

#### `map-event-trigger-records`

**Map event and trigger records** - The per-map event or trigger structure: tracked research places an eight-byte trigger record array at map record +0x10 with a count at +0x04 and a handler at 0x0800742C, while the decompiled object-array walk reads +0x04 as a pointer and counts from the structure it addresses.

- **Semantic read:** Tracked research documents reference the trigger family, and the SDK's script-ownership analysis reaches per-map script roots. No product reader enumerates trigger records as records.
- **Existing-record edit:** None.
- **New-record authoring:** None. Authored behaviour attaches through the placement behaviour path instead, which is a different mechanism.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Map record to script roots; the disputed handler 0x0800742C to the 0x18 rectangle object.
- **Raw backing range:** Claimed at map record +0x10; not independently bounded.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable: no write path exists.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None.
- **Known restrictions:** The evidence conflicts on the map record's own layout, so the boundary is not established. The strongest measured statement is that the object-array mechanism is reached through a pointer at map record +0x04, which is not compatible with a count byte at the same offset.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to settle the offset conflict by reading the consumer's arithmetic, then a runtime probe on a map with a live event.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge MINIMAL, runtime NEEDED, confidence UNKNOWN); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** docs/research/BUU_MAP_EVENT_REFERENCES.md and docs/research/BUU_MAP_DIALOG_SEMANTICS.md (tracked claims); FUN_08008b30 decompilation (contradicting structure); no trigger symbol name exists in the image
- **Open research questions:** Is +0x04 a count or a pointer? Is there a separate eight-byte trigger family, or is the trigger family the same array the placements live in?
- **Evidence references:** FUN_08008b30 (ROM decompilation); docs/research/BUU_MAP_EVENT_REFERENCES.md; docs/research/BUU_MAP_DIALOG_SEMANTICS.md; 0x0800742C (claimed handler)

### Entities and gameplay

#### `placement-records`

**Placement-family object records** - The object family the SDK models, reached from the first per-area array: records whose lead word is the constructor wrapper 0x0800FD55 and which carry a sprite id read at +0x10 and handed to the sprite-id resolver.

- **Semantic read:** Placements enumerate per map with their stored signed position; supported types are classified; unsupported types render read-only.
- **Existing-record edit:** Position moves through the proven signed map-pixel contract with an explicit signed-16 guard. Runtime-proven.
- **New-record authoring:** Clone-only: an authored entity is a configured clone of a supported existing type; 268 maps are clone-capable; 255 slots per map is the ceiling because the count is one byte.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Placement to sprite identity (identity of the drawn sprite is not proven), placement to behaviour attachment, placement to the enemy stat table through the factory's literal 0x0800FD75 = 0x08711274.
- **Raw backing range:** Records are scattered across the object-array span from file 0x0728FC upward; no contiguous table and no stride: the codec is factory-led and variable-length.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate plus build; the authored entity and its slot resolution are runtime-proven.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Objects mode; Scene editor opened from the placement.
- **Known restrictions:** Clone-only authoring. Placement-to-sprite identity is not proven, so markers are neutral and browsing cannot say which sprite an object uses. The profile declares placement selector maximum 149 while the independently verified enemy-stat extent is 141 records, so selectors 141..149 name targets outside any verified codec.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra for the unmodelled fields and the enemy-to-sprite link; hex editor otherwise.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x0800FD55 and the constructor FUN_0800f68c; the field read at 0x0800F6AE (ldr r0,[r5,#0x10]) and the call at 0x0800F6B0; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:34-44
- **Open research questions:** Which fields of a placement record beyond the sprite id and position are read by the engine? What resolves an enemy's sprite at runtime? The construction site writes actor+0x1A0 with 40 of 40 rows matched, while the vertical field actor+0x1A4 and the facing selector 0x03001A34 are unproven: a fresh-map-load run would close them.
- **Evidence references:** 0x0800FD55 (ROM bytes); FUN_0800f68c at 0x0800F6AE; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:34-44; tools/research/domain_reachability.py (placement types); docs/research/PLACEMENT_POSITION_PROVENANCE.md

#### `sibling-object-record-families`

**Unmodelled sibling object record families (two families)** - Two further object families sharing the per-area array mechanism: records whose lead words are 0x08017DA3 (191 sprite-bearing records reported) and 0x080111A9 (148 reported), the third family at that address family being the placements of the row placement-records. Each is proven to load one field and call the same sprite resolver.

- **Semantic read:** No product reader. The sprite id field offset is proven for each family (+0x10 and +0x0C) and nothing else is decoded.
- **Existing-record edit:** None.
- **New-record authoring:** None.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Both families call the sprite-id resolver FUN_08000158; the containing array is one of the three unmodelled per-area arrays.
- **Raw backing range:** Not bounded. No stride and no table were found for either family.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable: no write path exists.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None.
- **Known restrictions:** The record lengths, the record counts and every field except the sprite id are unknown for both families, which is why the state is UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED rather than KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED: a proven field offset is not a proven boundary. The counts 191 and 148 come from tracked research and were not re-derived in this census.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra with byte-level verification, plus runtime observation to see when each family is constructed.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PARTIAL, runtime NEEDED, confidence INFERRED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM disassembly at 0x08017DA6 (ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; bl 0x08000158) and 0x080111AC (ldr r0,[r0,#0xc]; bl 0x08000158); counts from docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md:36-48, which proves three leading words over 1,898 slots, and are not re-derived
- **Open research questions:** What are these families: decorations, projectiles, interactive props, spawn points? Which per-area array reaches each one, and what bounds either family's records?
- **Evidence references:** 0x08017DA2 (ROM disassembly); 0x080111A8 (ROM disassembly); docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md:36-48

#### `enemy-stat-records`

**Enemy and character stat records** - The 141-record, 28-byte stat table the placement factory indexes: a per-record id field, a shared pointer and a per-record pointer into a variable pool.

- **Semantic read:** All 141 records of 28 bytes enumerate with field decode, round-trip and a CLI listing.
- **Existing-record edit:** Fields are rewritable in place through the SDK and its CLI, and the packaged enemy randomizer rewrites fields in place with a changed-field list. No Workbench surface reaches the stat tables, and no capability in the registry names them.
- **New-record authoring:** Not meaningful: the count is fixed and no growth path for a stat record is claimed.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Placement factory to stat table; enemy stats to the character-sprite table is NOT established: no enemy record holds a pointer into the graphics regions and no field indexes the 297-entry table, so the selection happens in code.
- **Raw backing range:** file 0x711274..0x7121E0 = image 0x08711274..0x087121E0, 3,948 bytes, 141 x 28.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Stat round-trip tests exist; in-place field writes build into the image. A LOGII stat codec does not exist and the profile states no LOGII table matches these record shapes.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None in the Workbench; the packaged enemy randomizer has its own window.
- **Known restrictions:** Field semantics are named by the product for the fields it models: tools/webfoot/stats.py:76-93 defines the enemy fields exp, hp, level, strength, power and endurance, with level bounded 1..200 from a disassembled comparison in the experience award path, and stats.py:231 exposes a lookup by hp. The residual gaps are the unnamed pointer and pool fields, the byte pairs, and the absence of runtime proof that an edited value is consumed. The profile declares placement selector maximum 149 while this extent holds 141 records, so selectors 141..149 point outside any verified codec. Runtime evidence is PARTIAL and the gap is named: the enemy randomizer's recorded runs read the engine's own MapEntry+0x14 slots and two reward counters, but the record states the run does not read a constructed actor.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to name the fields through the damage formula; mGBA debugger to confirm a changed value is read.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime PARTIAL, confidence INFERRED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence INFERRED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x08711274 with the recurring pointer at a 7-word period; the base literal 0x0801BA90 = 0x08711274; tools/webfoot/stats.py; tools/webfoot/formats/stat_tables.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:49-52
- **Open research questions:** Which field feeds the damage formula? What does the shared 0x08708920 pointer name?
- **Evidence references:** 0x08711274 (ROM bytes); 0x0801BA90 literal = 0x08711274; tools/webfoot/stats.py; tools/webfoot/formats/stat_tables.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:49-52; tools/research/domain_reachability.py

**Playable-character base stats** - Nine records of nine halfwords at 0x086FDA4C: three leading stat values, five byte-pair fields and a trailing zero. Nine records matches the plausible party size.

- **Semantic read:** All nine records of 18 bytes enumerate through the same stat module and CLI.
- **Existing-record edit:** Fields are rewritable in place through the SDK and CLI. No Workbench surface.
- **New-record authoring:** Not meaningful at nine fixed records.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** The only inbound reference is a parameter literal inside the unnamed function at 0x08004904, so the consumer is located but not named.

- **Validation and rebuild:** Round-trip is covered by the stat module's tests. In-place edits build into the image.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None.
- **Known restrictions:** The product names the character fields it models: tools/webfoot/stats.py:76-93 defines level, hp, ep, strength, power, endurance and speed. What is not established is the byte-pair fields' meaning, whether they are growth rates or resistances, and whether level-up deltas live in this table at all, so it may be base-only.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to decompile 0x08004904; mGBA to watch a stat change on level-up.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence INFERRED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x086FDA4C; tools/webfoot/stats.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:53-56; tools/research/domain_reachability.py:394
- **Open research questions:** Where do level-up deltas live? Which halfword is which stat?
- **Evidence references:** 0x086FDA4C (ROM bytes); 0x08004904 (unnamed consumer); tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:53-56

#### `items-and-inventory`

**Item table** - The 83-record, 52-byte item table at 0x083BD2F8 with a class bit, four text indices, a price, and two out-pointers into per-item pools, plus the two item index lists an engine consumer builds.

- **Semantic read:** No product reader enumerates items as items. The SDK reaches this table only as the static owner of the item_use script family, where the four halfwords at +0x02..+0x08 are proven text indices read through the text pointer table.
- **Existing-record edit:** None as items. Item-owned scripts are not authored.
- **New-record authoring:** None.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Item record +0x30 to its script in the item_use family (23 of 83 non-null); +0x02..+0x08 to the text table; the two index lists FUN_080164d0 builds are the closest thing to an inventory structure found.
- **Raw backing range:** file 0x3BD2F8..0x3BE3D4 = image 0x083BD2F8..0x083BE3D4, 4,316 bytes, 83 x 52. Sub-pools: 33-byte pool at 0x083BBBB0, 703 bytes; variable pool at 0x083BBE70; 20-byte-stride table at 0x083BB78C.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable at this state. The item-owned script corpus re-encodes byte-identically, which is a script-codec result, not an item-editing result.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None. The item table appears in the Atlas only through research artifacts.
- **Known restrictions:** Field semantics beyond the class bit, the price and the four text indices are not established; the repeating 16-byte block at +0x0C..+0x20 is unexplained; the 33-byte pool has no found consumer, so its element shape beyond the stride is unconstrained; the inventory itself has no located structure. The inventory is not established as a ROM structure: the two item index lists the consumer FUN_080164d0 builds live at +0x134 and +0x284 of a runtime object, so they are runtime state rather than an editable ROM domain.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to find the consumer of the 33-byte pool and to name +0x0C..+0x20; hex editor otherwise.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)

- **Open research questions:** Where does the inventory live at runtime, and is it ROM-initiated? What are the 33-byte records?

#### `enemy-behaviour-data`

**Enemy behaviour data** - The per-actor movement, aggression and reaction logic behind the placed objects. The product can attach an authored script to an authored entity; the engine's own behaviour data and interpreter are not modelled.

- **Semantic read:** None as behaviour data. The product reads a placement's wander box for authoring purposes.
- **Existing-record edit:** None.
- **New-record authoring:** Only through the behaviour attachment row, which writes a script rather than behaviour data.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Placement record to wherever its behaviour parameters live, unestablished; the stat table to the damage the actor's attacks do, unestablished.
- **Raw backing range:** Not established.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** None.
- **Known restrictions:** The boundary is unknown: it is not established whether behaviour is data-driven per actor, code-driven per type, or both, so the state is UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED rather than KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED. A negative search over the declared tables is not a proven boundary.
- **External tool currently required:** mGBA debugger to trace an actor's decision, which is the cheapest route; Ghidra afterwards.

#### `behaviour-attachment-authoring`

**Engine trigger and effect contract family** - The engine's trigger and effect contracts that an authored entity can be attached to: the trigger receivers the script VM dispatches through, and the native effect handlers a script can invoke. The product reaches exactly one trigger contract and one effect through it, which is the measured subset, not the family.

- **Semantic read:** The script-ownership analysis reads which records own which script roots; the product shows an authored entity's attached behaviour.
- **Existing-record edit:** An attached script can be replaced through the project.
- **New-record authoring:** A straight-line script can be authored, with no branches and no native calls, attached to one proven trigger contract and one proven effect; the engine has executed the authored bytes and rendered the result.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Authored entity to script body to effect to trigger; the trigger selector is checked against the clone source's qualification.
- **Raw backing range:** The authored script body is allocated above the original ROM end or in the declared 256-byte window when it fits.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate refuses anything outside the proven contract; build emits the script and the placement expansion; runtime-proven.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Maps editor Objects mode and the Scene editor.
- **Known restrictions:** One trigger out of the engine's whole set is offered, one effect is proven, no branches and no native calls, and the trigger is only offered when the clone source qualifies. A map cannot receive both a new actor and an authored placement expansion.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra for the remaining trigger and effect contracts, which is what would widen this row.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/authored_placements.py:144,226; tools/webfoot/data/behavior_triggers.py; tools/webfoot/data/script_effects.py; runtime observations in src/data/capabilities.json:269-282
- **Open research questions:** What is the concrete action target for the trigger-family receivers the script VM cannot name?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/authored_placements.py:144,226; tools/webfoot/data/behavior_triggers.py; src/data/capabilities.json:269-282; docs/journeys/scene-authoring.md:88-98

### Script and text

#### `script-bytecode-vm`

**Script bytecode and interpreter** - The engine's script VM: an opcode byte fetched by the interpreter at 0x08004038, indexed through the primary dispatch table at 0x080554C0, with 266 native handlers. The product reads, disassembles and assembles a subset.

- **Semantic read:** Both Buu families disassemble with opcode widths, ownership and tiling verified against the canonical image; the LOGII family is declared with its own encoding (stack_be7_v1) and is readable.
- **Existing-record edit:** Buu script bodies are rewritable in place within their pool; there is no general script editor and no instruction-level authoring surface.
- **New-record authoring:** A straight-line effect script only, through the behaviour attachment path. No new script root can be created.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Script root to owning record; opcode to native handler; item and static40 records to their script slots.
- **Raw backing range:** Buu static40 roots tile the 548-byte pool at 0x08720340; item_use roots tile the 703-byte pool at 0x083BBBB0. LOGII: 539-byte pool at 0x086D66C0.
- **Validation and rebuild:** The corpus re-encodes byte-identically for both Buu families; validate refuses an unsupported form. LOGII has no proven write path.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Scene editor shows an attached script's body; no VM-level editor.
- **Known restrictions:** The game-level meaning of most of the 266 native handlers is unknown, which is what blocks general script authoring and LOGII dialogue. Buu's static40 corpus contains no branch opcode, so the branch contract rests on handler disassembly; the item_use corpus does exercise branches 0x12 and 0x13.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra over the handler table and the dispatch veneer; decomp repo for orientation.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PARTIAL, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/formats/script_vm.py and tools/webfoot/scripts.py; docs/research/BUU_SCRIPT_VM.md; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:85-137
- **Open research questions:** What do the 266 handlers do at the game level? Which opcodes can an authored script safely use?
- **Evidence references:** 0x08004038 (interpreter); 0x080554C0 (dispatch table, 31 slots); tools/webfoot/formats/script_vm.py; docs/research/BUU_SCRIPT_VM.md:55-63; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:85-137,223-232

#### `script-tables`

**Script root tables** - The pointer tables that index script roots: Buu's static40 (40 x 16 at 0x08720564 with slots 4, 8 and 12) and item_use (83 x 52 at 0x083BD2F8 with slot 48), and LOGII's static43 (43 x 16 at 0x086D68DC with slots 4 and 8).

- **Semantic read:** All three tables enumerate; every pointer is non-null, distinct and strictly ascending for the Buu families; the LOGII family is declared with its encoding.
- **Existing-record edit:** Roots are rewritable in place within the pools. Table growth is not supported: static40 is exactly 40 records and retail sits at the bound.
- **New-record authoring:** No new script roots.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Table slot to root; owning record to slot; the walker 0x080141EE forms table + 16 x i for the Buu static40 family.
- **Raw backing range:** Buu static40 file 0x720564, 640 bytes; item_use file 0x3BD2F8, 4,316 bytes; LOGII static43 file 0x6D68DC, stride 16.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Both Buu corpora re-encode byte-identically and the pools are exhaustively tiled; validate refuses an unsupported form.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Scene editor for the authored case only.
- **Known restrictions:** Fixed capacity with no growth path for any family; each family's table has no count word, so the bound lives in compiled instructions. Relocatable is false for every family because no verified free region is declared for those profiles.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to find a growth path, which is where the compiled bounds live; otherwise hex editor.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PARTIAL, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:85-137 and :223-232; tools/webfoot/scripts.py; tools/research/domain_reachability.py:325-331
- **Open research questions:** What would a growth path cost for static40, whose bound is a compiled comparison?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:85-137,223-232; 0x080141EE (walker); tools/research/domain_reachability.py:325-331

#### `text-string-tables`

**Text string tables** - The pointer table and NUL-terminated pool that hold the game's ordinary strings: Buu's 1,534 UTF-16LE entries in an 82,874-byte pool at 0x0805792C, and LOGII's 260 ASCII entries in a 5,184-byte pool at 0x080E2C50.

- **Semantic read:** Buu's table and pool tile exhaustively with no gap or overlap and each of the 1,534 pointers resolves to a string start; LOGII's 260 pointers name all 246 distinct targets and its pool tiles exhaustively.
- **Existing-record edit:** An existing id is rewritten; a replacement longer than its record is placed in verified writable space and the owning entry repointed, gated per table by declared capability and per entry by measured single-reference ownership. Buu is runtime-proven. LOGII has an application-proof write path: tests/integration/test_logii_text_rom.py:386-422 builds a LOGII image with an edited string and asserts the exact seven differing bytes, with relocation refused and no free region declared. No LOGII runtime observation exists.
- **New-record authoring:** New text-table ids are not claimed for any title. A 1,535th Buu entry would require rewriting 51 code references.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** 43 inbound references for the Buu table; item records index the table through their text halfwords at +0x02..+0x08; Atlas indexes strings including inside compressed containers.
- **Raw backing range:** Buu pool file 0x05792C..0x06BCE6, table file 0x06BCE8..0x06D4E0. LOGII pool 0x080E2C50..0x080E4090, table at 0x080E2840.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Buu relocation is proven through build and runtime; five Buu entries (indices 689, 818, 819, 856, 1342) carry a second aligned word and are refused per entry rather than by a list. LOGII relocation is false.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Inspector edits dialogue lines, which is the dialogue row; ordinary strings have no Workbench surface.
- **Known restrictions:** No new ids. Buu's display width still limits a centred long line. LOGII's table aliases, so its pointers are neither unique nor strictly ascending and it has no relocation.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to widen the reference set beyond the 51 measured for the Buu table; otherwise none.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x0805792C and 0x0806BCE8 with 43 inbound references; tools/webfoot/text.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:61-84 and :233-255; tests/integration/test_logii_text_rom.py
- **Open research questions:** What is the complete reference set for a Buu text body outside the 51 measured table references?
- **Evidence references:** 0x0805792C (ROM bytes); 0x0806BCE8 (ROM bytes); tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:61-84,233-255; tools/research/domain_reachability.py:307-313; tests/integration/test_logii_text_rom.py

#### `dialogue-records`

**Dialogue records and containers** - The dialogue system itself: records reached through seven selectors and carried in compressed containers, distinct from the ordinary string tables.

- **Semantic read:** Mapped targets resolve; records can be enumerated, found by start offset and found by crossing offset. LOGII dialogue is a script-interleaved, partly compressed stream that the profile states cannot be enumerated without script-VM work.
- **Existing-record edit:** A mapped line is edited, validated and built. A replacement that changes decoded length re-authors the record's durable handle and re-lays out its container.
- **New-record authoring:** Not claimed: the product rewrites an existing record, it does not create a new dialogue id.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Line to owning map or event; dialogue to its container; Atlas and the Inspector share the target registry.
- **Raw backing range:** Containers are reached by seven selectors; the emitted pointer for one observed case lives at 0x08800000 in a generated 16 MiB image.
- **Validation and rebuild:** A container whose records cross the edited one is refused; the rebuilt container must stay inside the toolkit's 64 KiB decoded-container limit. Runtime-proven: the retail dialogue box displayed a longer authored line wrapped across two lines.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Inspector mapped dialogue line editing.
- **Known restrictions:** One record at a time: registered targets hold a single record. The retail container nearly fills the 64 KiB decoded limit, so this target's ceiling is a 94-byte line. LOGII dialogue is unsupported by declaration.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra over the script VM for LOGII dialogue; hex editor for unmapped containers.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge MINIMAL, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence INFERRED); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/dialogue.py:107,244; tools/webfoot/compressed_dialogue.py:155,185,233; tools/webfoot/formats/webfoot_lz.py; runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:111-126
- **Open research questions:** What would a batch re-layout cost for two records in one container?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/dialogue.py:107,244; tools/webfoot/compressed_dialogue.py:155,185,233; src/data/capabilities.json:111-126; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:262-269

#### `event-resource-pool-and-index`

**Event resource pool and its index** - The engine's event or script resource store: a 522-entry, 2,088-byte pointer table at 0x0879B704 whose entries are strictly ascending pointers into a 127,328-byte pool from 0x0877C5A4 to 0x0879B704. Six small accessor functions sit in the code around 0x080030da..0x080032b4, one per query kind.

- **Semantic read:** The index enumerates and the product resolves event_resource identities through the Atlas and the CLI, so a display path exists by name.
- **Existing-record edit:** None. No writer addresses the pool or the index.
- **New-record authoring:** None. Resource element boundaries are not established, so nothing in the span can be re-emitted.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Index entry to pool element; the Atlas resolves event_resource identities; the pool carries at least one embedded Thumb literal pool, so it is not pure data.
- **Raw backing range:** index file 0x79B704..0x79BF2C = image 0x0879B704, 2,088 bytes, 522 x 4; pool file 0x77C5A4..0x79B704 = 127,328 bytes.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable at this state: no writer. A tracked record asserts the records tile the pool exhaustively; see the conflict recorded in restrictions.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Atlas lists event_resource objects; no editor surface.
- **Known restrictions:** Two tracked records conflict and the ledger must not merge them: tiling proves the EXTENT (that the pool has no uncovered bytes between resource starts), while the INTERNAL layout of each variable-length element is not recovered, so element boundaries that a writer would need are still unknown. The pool also contains embedded Thumb code, which is why a reader must not treat it as a pure data blob.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra to decode one element's internal structure; a custom script to enumerate it today.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x0879B704 (first 16 words are in-image ascending pointers); tools/webfoot/atlas_producers/seed.py:652-679; tools/webfoot/data/placement_contracts.py:16-39; tools/webfoot/formats/placement_links.py:209; docs/research/BUU_EVENT_RESOURCE.md; tests/integration/test_buu_event_resource_rom.py
- **Open research questions:** What is the internal layout of one resource element? Which accessor corresponds to which query kind?
- **Evidence references:** 0x0879B704 (ROM bytes); 0x0877C5A4 (pool); tools/webfoot/atlas_producers/seed.py:652-679; tools/webfoot/cli.py:1800-1823; tests/integration/test_buu_event_resource_rom.py

### Graphics

#### `actor-sprite-registry`

**Actor sprite identity registry** - The 297-entry character-sprite pointer table at 0x086B6BDC and the resolver that indexes it, plus the per-identity structure whose +0x54 word walks to animations.

- **Semantic read:** All 297 entries resolve; ascending pointers are verified; animation walking reaches 1,017 animation objects, 10,980 frame records and 7,390 container offsets. The sprite browser draws one piece per direction slot.
- **Existing-record edit:** Palette recolour and graphics import reach the art; identity fields are not editable in place.
- **New-record authoring:** A new sprite identity can be created from a donor, one per image, appended above the original end and runtime-observed resolving and drawing. The surface is application-proof while the underlying mechanism was runtime-observed.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Placement records and the two sibling families call the resolver; the resolver reaches the identity's animation list; Atlas lists the owners.
- **Raw backing range:** table file 0x6B6BDC..0x6B7080 = image 0x086B6BDC..0x086B7080, 1,188 bytes, 297 x 4.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate refuses donor, sheet, geometry and template problems; build allocates and relocates; the authored identity was runtime-observed.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Graphics editor Sprites tab: browse, animation stepping, palette recolour, authored sprite New/Edit/Remove.
- **Known restrictions:** At most one new identity per image, because an appended identity grows the registry and repoints the two words that name it. Every authored frame copies the donor's own first frame, so the frame-composition budget is unchanged rather than modelled. The four direction slots' screen meaning is unresolved project-wide. The Buu table is not at the same offset in either sibling: at file offset 0x6B6BDC LOG1 holds 0x88888890 and zeros and LOGII holds bitmap-shaped noise. That refutes same-offset sharing of the Buu table and measures nothing about either sibling's own sprite system, so the LOGII and LOG1 cells stay not investigated.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra for the identity structure's remaining fields; a custom script for bulk identity work.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM disassembly of FUN_08000158 at 0x0800015A with the literal 0x080003C0 = 0x086B6BDC; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:15-33; tools/webfoot/sprite_identity.py
- **Open research questions:** What are the two header words the surface carries but does not author? What do the sub-10 resolver ids select? Bookkeeping defect: the capability registry's sprite-new proof field reads application while its own evidence names a runtime parity run on an as-authored production image, so the registry proof level is stale, not the coverage.
- **Evidence references:** FUN_08000158 at 0x0800015A; 0x080003C0 literal = 0x086B6BDC; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:15-33; src/data/capabilities.json:315-334; docs/research/SPRITE_NEW_ATTACHMENT_RUNTIME_PARITY.md

#### `appearance-records`

**Appearance records** - The 232-record, 16-byte appearance table at 0x0874D380 that binds a character to an on-screen name and description; the Scouter's character screen reads it.

- **Semantic read:** All 232 records enumerate; the five literal-bound words are published as an absolute ROM reference document.
- **Existing-record edit:** Existing records are editable through the project, with an explicit opt-in to take over a sprite id a canonical record already selects.
- **New-record authoring:** New records are appended above the original end and the whole table is re-emitted, supporting 232 to 240. Runtime-observed: a driven session saw the retail search return an authored record for a retail actor and the character screen display the authored name and description.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Appearance to sprite id; appearance to the seen-flag array; the roster structure the engine builds from the seen flags is relocated with the table.
- **Raw backing range:** file 0x74D380..0x74E200, 3,712 bytes, 232 x 16.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Validate refuses a takeover that was not asked for and refuses ids a negative-stat record selects; build re-emits the table and restates the twenty-nine compiled statements of the roster layout.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Graphics editor: Authored appearance New/Edit/Remove.
- **Known restrictions:** Growth is capped at eight added records because the seen-bit array is 232 bits and its initializer zeroes a word just after it. New text ids are not available, so an authored definition shares an existing on-screen name. The post-canonical seen-flag write and the roster display-list builder were not observed on the final build.
- **External tool currently required:** Ghidra for the roster builder at 0x08024F3C; mGBA to observe the seen-flag write.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM bytes at 0x0874D380; tools/webfoot/appearances.py; tools/webfoot/appearance_authoring.py; runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:335-356

#### `sprite-frame-records`

**Sprite frames, pieces and graphics payloads** - The frame records behind a sprite identity: an 8-byte frame header with 12-byte piece records carrying stored pixel extents, whose containers hold the compressed pixel payload.

- **Semantic read:** Frames, pieces and containers decode; every container decodes and each decoded length equals the width by height its piece record independently declares; 7,390 container offsets are reachable by a piece.
- **Existing-record edit:** An extracted sprite asset's PNG can be edited and rebuilt, same dimensions only. No pixel editor exists: the workflow is extract, edit the PNG, validate, build.
- **New-record authoring:** Replacement only within the original topology; a new frame layout is not authorable and the frame-composition budget is copied from a donor.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Identity to animation to frame to piece to container; Atlas lists the owners of a container.
- **Raw backing range:** 1,017 animation objects, 10,980 frame records and 11,005 piece records are reachable; the container span 0x083C34D0..0x086A87A8 is 3,035,864 bytes at medium confidence.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Every confirmed reference to a relocated payload is rewritten, but the published reference set is not claimed complete. Only the expanded case was proven in the running engine.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Graphics editor Sprites tab browses and steps; import is a project workflow rather than a pixel surface.
- **Known restrictions:** Same dimensions only: dimensions, frame layout and topology are fixed. Actor-sprite graphics only. The re-encoder is not competitive, so a payload that no longer fits its slot is relocated and the build may emit a 16 MiB image. A container that no piece references is invisible to the product.
- **External tool currently required:** a standalone graphics editor for pixel work; a custom decoder plus the missing encoder for containers with no referring piece.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime PROVEN, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/formats/sprite_graphics.py; docs/research/GRAPHICS_FORMAT.md; src/data/capabilities.json:443-447 (research-only record of the frame layout); runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:299-314
- **Open research questions:** Which containers have no referring piece, and what reaches them?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/formats/sprite_graphics.py; docs/research/GRAPHICS_FORMAT.md; src/data/capabilities.json:299-314,443-447; 3,035,864-byte container span at 0x083C34D0

#### `animation-records`

**Animation records** - The per-frame animation data behind a sprite: the 24-byte records of three signed pairs indexed as base + 24 x animation + 8 x frame, with a 40-frame counter.

- **Semantic read:** The product reads and steps animations and draws one piece per direction slot.
- **Existing-record edit:** None. No frame timing, delay, piece count, tile index or frame geometry is authorable.
- **New-record authoring:** None, beyond accepting a donor's frames in the new-identity path.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Identity to animation pointer at structure +0x54; animation record to frame offsets.
- **Raw backing range:** Records begin at file 0x71E024 = image 0x0871E024, 24 bytes per record with an 8-byte element; the upper bound is unknown.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Not applicable: no write path.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Graphics editor animation stepping.
- **Known restrictions:** Whether the six dwords are three (x, y) pairs or two (x, y, z) triples is not decided; the sign and axis convention need runtime confirmation; the record count is unknown.
- **External tool currently required:** mGBA to confirm the axis convention; Ghidra to bound the record count.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge SUBSTANTIAL, runtime NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION, confidence INFERRED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** ROM disassembly of FUN_0801b984 with the literal 0x0801BA8C = 0x0871E024 and its multiply by 0x18; ROM bytes at 0x0871E024
- **Open research questions:** Three pairs or two triples? What is the animation record count and where does it end?
- **Evidence references:** FUN_0801b984 (ROM decompilation); 0x0801BA8C literal = 0x0871E024; 0x0871E024 (ROM bytes)

#### `object-palettes`

**Object palettes** - The shared object palette at 0x0805652C and the background palette at 0x0805632C that sprite and background graphics resolve through, plus the colour lookup block at 0x0805672C.

- **Semantic read:** Palette entries decode and the product shows which records refer to a palette; the object palette has 16 references against the background palette's one.
- **Existing-record edit:** One shared object palette entry is recolourable through the project; the SDK owns RGB-to-GBA packing and applies it at build.
- **New-record authoring:** Not meaningful: entries are recoloured, not created.
- **Cross-reference and navigation:** Sprite identity to palette; map layer to palette; Atlas reference counts distinguish shared from private palettes.
- **Raw backing range:** object palette file 0x05652C, 512 bytes; background palette file 0x05632C, 512 bytes; colour lookup block file 0x05672C, 4,608 bytes.
- **Validation and rebuild:** Proven at the emitted-ROM level by rendering the built image. An emulator run of the recolour was not performed, so this row is not FULLY_EDITABLE.
- **Current product and UI exposure:** Graphics editor palette recolour with an undoable command.
- **Known restrictions:** One entry at a time; no arbitrary graphics replacement; the recolour's runtime effect is unobserved. Two tracked sources disagree on the background palette address (0x080701B0 in the profile against 0x0805632C in the region map and the graphics coverage matrix), which is an open documentation defect.
- **External tool currently required:** none for the supported recolour; hex editor beyond it.
- **Per-game state:** Buu's Fury = PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (basis MEASURED, engine knowledge PROVEN, runtime NOT_NEEDED_FOR_CLASSIFICATION, confidence CONFIRMED); LOGII = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN); LOG1 = UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED (basis NOT_INVESTIGATED, engine knowledge UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN)
- **Evidence authority:** tools/webfoot/graphics.py:431,487-506; tools/webfoot/graphics_authoring.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:19-20; the decomp region map classifies both palettes as proven
- **Open research questions:** Which address is the background palette the engine loads?
- **Evidence references:** tools/webfoot/graphics.py:431,487-506; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:19-20; src/data/capabilities.json:127-139; 0x0805632C / 0x0805652C / 0x0805672C
